slides.title: Design one useful dashboard
slides.lead: Combine at least three views inside y=46…221.
points: Live signal: one or more chart traces
Derived value: tilt or vibration metric
Status: a readable OK / warning / alarm indicator
slides.notes: This is an optional practice challenge, with no grades or required submission. A machine-state classifier would require suitable machine data, not the gesture model.

slides.title: Make the budget testable
slides.lead: Target at least 8 screen updates/s with live data and one tap action.
points: Draw only changed regions; preserve firmware title, tabs and footer
Print d.stats and measure commands per update
Add a tap to reset counters, change threshold or change chart range
slides.notes: The challenge target comes from mini-challenge.md. Offline browser frame rate does not demonstrate meeting it.

slides.title: Explain a result with evidence
slides.lead: Use the self-check and compare your predictions with measurements.
points: 20 ms period; 0.5 Hz bins for 2 s; 25 Hz Nyquist
Dirty rectangles reduce work; thresholds trade accepted and missed events
Report source mode, units, time window and where processing ran
slides.notes: Ask each group for one observation, the code line that explains it, and one limitation. Revisit the eight questions in checkpoint.md.

slides.title: From visible data to an engineering decision
points: Browser: simulations and exact bundled synthetic CSV values
Host: Python analysis, model inference and drawing logic
MCU: real sensor acquisition, display operations and touch
Next extension: standalone firmware, with equivalent preprocessing and measured timing
slides.notes: Close by returning to the architecture. Assign the optional dashboard challenge for independent practice; keep reference slides available after class.
